title: दसवीं शादी
logline: Kiran shows the room two unopened folds and the real numbers, and the gang stops obeying Mausi; Mausi bares the scar to Aditya to turn him on her, and Kiran takes the keys, sends him home alive with nothing, and by evening is teaching the next bride to pour.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.

characters.name: किरण (Kiran)
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride. Tonight she faked the fatal dose; by evening she runs the bureau.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, a closed, watchful mouth. Low bun, sindoor, small red bindi, thin gold ring in the left nostril, block henna on both hands. b1 to b7: plain sindoor-red saree with a thin gold border, barefoot, red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms; from b4 the LEFT stack is pushed up toward the elbow and the crescent scar stays bare (story_locks.scar), she never pulls it down; from b6 Mausi's steel key ring is knotted at her left hip. b9 to b10 (period 3): plain ash-grey salwar-kurta and grey dupatta, both forearms bare with faint pressure lines where the bangles sat, the crescent on the outer LEFT forearm, the key ring at her left hip.
characters.voice_note: Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Hindi with everyday English (police, complaint, bureau, check, same). Kiran's register: low, flat, quick, short sentences, तू to Billu, तुम to Aditya, आप-forms to and about Mausi. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. By the bureau scene her pace has slowed into Mausi's unhurried warmth.

characters.name: आदित्य (Aditya Verma)
characters.role: The groom. Mohit's brother. Pretended to drink the dose; tonight he sees the hand and can do nothing with it.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, neat left-parted black hair, rimless rectangular glasses on in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta and churidar, creased; barefoot in the bedroom, tan leather sandals on the stairs and in the lane. Brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red thread outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken, educated small-city Hindi in full sentences. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; never shouts. The one place the voice may catch is the single word in b5.

characters.name: शकुन मौसी (Shakun Mausi)
characters.role: Owner of the bureau. Ordered Aditya's death tonight. Loses the keys and is set to writing the accounts.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened smile, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked hair in a tight oiled bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, mustard blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers, a dozen green glass bangles on each wrist. Steel ring of about eight keys at her LEFT hip in b1 to b5; none from b6 on.
characters.voice_note: Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Hindi-heavy. An endearment in every second line. Never raises her voice: the colder the move, the softer and slower she gets. Fully voiced, never a whisper.

characters.name: बिल्लू (Billu)
characters.role: Mausi's driver and the bride's 'brother'. Learns in numbers how long he has been short-changed and stops obeying her.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry, brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket, sleeves pushed up, over a black T-shirt; dark jeans; grey-white sneakers. Wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth until b3, when he takes it out; out for the rest of the episode. Car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, Bundelkhand street Hindi, Hindi-heavy. When surprised he goes loud for one line, then looks to Mausi. Once the numbers land, his pace drops and the jokes stop.

characters.name: लड़के (the boys)
characters.look: Never a face. Two fixed shapes: heavy-set, shaved head, maroon track jacket; thin, checked shirt, cloth cap. Backs, hands, boots and backlit silhouettes only, heads cropped, turned away or in full shadow.
characters.voice_note: No lines. Any breath or shuffle is a sound effect.

characters.name: छोटी (Chhoti)
characters.role: The next bride. Her first wedding is tomorrow.
characters.look: Adult woman, 19, about 5 ft 1, slight, wide curious eyes, light-brown skin. One long black braid pulled forward over her right shoulder. Plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta, white salwar, a plain dupatta (D-007 direction 14). Henna finished on both palms. Kiran's red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms. Phone in a plain pink cover in her right hand.
characters.voice_note: Female, 19, a young woman's voice, not a child's: bright, quick, sing-song, a giggle in the breath. Here the giggle is put on over fear.

location: Four places: the rented house's bedroom (b1 to b6), its stairwell (b7) and the lane outside (b8) at dawn, then Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau's front room the same evening (b9 to b10).
time_of_day: Night 1, about 5:05 am to first light (b1 to b8). Bedroom light state 3 for b1 to b6 (amber lamp, the landing bulb through the open door, pre-dawn blue at the window grille, greying toward dawn by b6); first grey light in the stairwell (b7) and the lane (b8). Day 2, evening (b9 to b10).

On the sheet by Aditya's hip, the small black notebook, closed on the creased photograph, where Mausi left it (s1b01 b11). The engine starts as sound.

Bureau front room, day 2 evening: tube light, blue dusk at the roll-down shutter, shut to customers. Time overlay: 'शाम'. Set-up 1 (the 1.6 s silence): Mausi at the desk at the back of the room, writing in the red ledger, no keys at her hip; in the foreground, face out of frame, Kiran in the grey salwar-kurta, the key ring at her left hip, her bare left forearm with the crescent in the tube light. She giggles at Kiran; the fold trembles.

sfx_notes: Bed, b1 to b6: a shut lane before dawn, the lamp's faint hum, one dog far off. No rain.
b1: Mausi's keys chink once as she half turns on l02; the frame is Billu, so the chink alone carries her turn.
b2: Billu's sneakers on the concrete floor; a boot shifts by the door; the car key's steel ring ticks once on his finger on the key insert.
b3: marigold garlands rustle and the bed creaks as Aditya sits up; two pairs of boots step back on concrete toward the door.
b4: green glass bangles clink as Mausi grips the wrist; the chooda's dry slide up the forearm; two tiny paper ticks as the folds land on the sheet. Duck the bed under l15.
b6: the key ring unhooked from Mausi's hip, a long chink; a shorter chink as Kiran knots it at her own.
b7: stairwell echo, sandals on concrete steps, first birds through the open front door.
b8: dawn birds; Billu's car ignition turns, catches and idles, then pulls away. Nothing else.
b9: tube light hum; a ballpoint scratching on ledger paper from the desk, continuous under the scene.
b10: a paper tap on the fold, a soft hiss of powder into milk. The bed and music duck right down under l30 so every word is clear; after l30 only the pen scratch, then cut.
music_note: No score in b1 to b3. A low single-note drone enters on the wrist grab in b4 and holds through b5, gone by b6. b6 to b8 are sound only. A faint lullaby-like phrase enters under b9, ducks under l30 and ends unresolved on the final image.
ending_question: किरण जिस ज़िंदगी से निकलना चाहती थी, अब उसी की मालकिन है: क्या छोटी कल अपनी पहली शादी में पूरी पुड़िया डालेगी?
writer_notes: Sources: bible.json s1b03 beats b1 to b10, endings.B, story_locks and production_locks, read with D-003, D-005, D-007, D-008, D-013 and D-014. Where D-007 and the bible differ, D-007 governs. Revised after the critic's review (review-notes.json, score 7.9): all 4 must-fix items and all medium and minor items applied; see writer_response there.

Line ids: l31 is the new Billu line ('आठ।') and sits between l04 and l05 in play order. No existing id was renumbered, so the review's line references stay valid. Play order is the order in the beats array, not id order. No S4 ledger existed for s1b03 when this was written.

Length: 31 lines, about 946 dialogue characters with tags and the space after each tag excluded (hand count, code points, nukta counted separately), under D-007's 1,050 measure. Spoken targets 105.6 s, 20 speaker changes x 0.3 s = 6.0 s, silences 16.2 s: 127.8 s. Estimate: at the 8.4 characters a second measured on the proof's Hindi v4 takes, this projects to about 113 s spoken and about 135 s in all, at D-007's ceiling. If the first measured cut is over about 130 s, trim inside beats in this order: l02 (Mausi's 'चल बेटा, घर।' can go into l01's shot as silence), l13's second half, l19, l24. Do not cut l04, l31, l05 or l06 (D-007 direction 8 wants two weddings and Billu's own figures), l15, l18 or l30.

Locked and directed lines: l18 is the bible's own b6 line (kept_apart_in_the_two_finales). l15 keeps the bible's b4 anchor. l30 is D-007 direction 12 word for word, with 'हाथ मत काँपने दे।' in front of it as l29; writer_notes' 'identical' rule is superseded. 'आपने ही सिखाया है', 'the boy turned out weak', 'रेखा' and 'तुलसी' are not spoken. The 'since fourteen' appeal (l13) belongs to this episode only (D-007 direction 10).

D-007 direction 8: b2 covers two weddings (the seventh, then Mohit's, the sixth) and tonight, with one line for the rest (l07). Kiran asks and Billu says both of his own figures aloud (l31 'आठ', l06 'चार'), as he did for the last party in s1b02 l07. Numbers avoid चौदह, बारह, ग्यारह and अठारह, which are already spoken elsewhere for other things. l13 is the only place the tawa and the uncle's kitchen are spoken (story_locks.scar.origin).
D-007 advisory for b7 taken: l25 and l26. l23 and l24 use 'complaint' so the line echoes that Mohit filed none (characters.aditya.bio).

Short turns flagged for extra takes (writer_notes allows them, skill rule): l31 'आठ।', l16 'तुम।', l17 'हाँ। मैं।', l26 'कहाँ?'. If l16 is unstable after three takes, the voice director may try '[quietly] तुम... तुम थीं।' with the subtitle changed to match. [sharply] on l08 means low and fast, as in the proofs, not loud.

Mid-beat silences: in b3 Aditya sits up over the second sentence of l11, not in a gap; in b4 the chooda is shown already pushed up over the first sentence of l15. All silent_seconds therefore sit before or after the lines as marked.

Per-frame hold (production_locks 8 s ceiling with the Gate 0b overrun of 20 to 60 per cent): b1 set-up 2 holds l01 only; b2 cuts to the car-key insert on 'गाड़ी' and holds it through l08; b7's silence is its own frame and l22, l23, l24, l26 and l27 each have their own frame. The longest single-frame holds left are 5.6 s on targets (l01, l12, l21), about 7.3 s at a 30 per cent overrun and about 9 s at 60 per cent; if a measured take on any of them passes 8 s, the editor splits it with a 1.3x punch-in.

Frame budget (D-010, 28 generated frames an episode): frames marked REUSE or PUNCH-IN in b2, b5 and b7 are not new generations. The new car-key insert (b2), the b7 door frame, the b7 print insert and the b7 over-shoulder frame add four. Not recounted against 28; that count is an estimate for S7.

Faces per frame (D-007 direction 16): every set-up named in action holds at most two sheet faces. b9 and b10 keep Kiran's face out of the wide and keep the final image to hands with Mausi soft behind.

Production locks: the boys are boots, backs and silhouettes only and never speak; no weapon; no intimacy; Mohit is only the hand in the print; all readable text (the 'शाम' overlay, ledger rows) is overlay. Motion that cannot be a still (the car starting, powder falling, Mausi's half-turn in b1, the folds dropping in b4) is carried by sound or a single changed frame.

State for S4 and S7 (D-013 rule 3): light state 3 in b1 to b6, greying toward dawn by b6. On the sheet by Aditya's hip, the small black notebook, closed on the creased photograph, where Mausi left it (s1b01 b11), in b1 to b4; it has fallen open in b5 with the print half out of it. The folds are in Kiran's LEFT palm in b1 and b3, fall onto the sheet in b4 and lie beside the notebook and print in b5; they are not seen after b5. Kiran picks up notebook and print from the sheet between b6 and b7 (not shown); in b7 both are in her right hand, the print's back to camera. Billu's car key is on its steel ring on his right index finger throughout. The key ring is on Mausi's left hip in b1 to b5 and on Kiran's left hip from b6. From b4 Kiran's left stack stays pushed up and the scar stays bare. In b9 and b10 Chhoti's phone is in her right hand and the fold in her left; Kiran's left hand covers Chhoti's left. Aditya's grey phone stays in Billu's jacket from s1b01 b10 and is never returned: no shot in this episode or later shows it back with Aditya (ledger P18). Kiran rides out of frame in the front passenger seat in b8 (ledger P17).
Tags: only tags already used in the proof scenes. No whispers in this episode. l30, the cliffhanger image's line, is [calm] and unfiltered.

Not verified: the JSON was not run through a parser (this session has no shell); the character count, timing sums and speaker-change count are by hand; no line has been voiced and no frame generated. script.en.json does not exist yet.
